scope: CSP16.2: promote the packaged baseline through the fleet leader (promote-baseline command, leader executor, receipts, console surface, and the D42 promotion limits)
deviations_from_contract: The receipt key carries the hash tag of the deployment keys so the request, the lease, and the receipt share one Valkey slot.
The leader executes requests in a separate executePromotions goroutine signaled at the end of Renew, not inside the Renew call.
A leader that loses the lease before the outcome leaves the request pending for the next leader. The contract named a 'lease moved' refusal. The documentation now states the pending behavior.
A refused outcome is not durable. A retry with the same operation ID evaluates the request again.
The observer refuses every shared write and does not replay the fleet. Starmap schedules run in observe mode from open to Close (1.08 s pure, 19.8 s race) and stop at the lease check.
AcquireLease is refused before storage in observe mode, so the refused-write counter does not count it.
The test memory store has a one-time loseLeaseBefore hook on the head-initialized key for the lost-lease test.
Commit 5dc4cb7f carries the cli: prefix but also changes internal/app.
recorded_limits: A receipt write that fails after the head commits leaves the request pending. A re-run of the same operation reports a refused receipt because the head already moved.
A forged baseline replaces a retained one only through the lease holder, per decision 16.2-9.
A local deployment refuses both commands with ErrBaselinePromotionFleetOnly. The commands require Valkey and PostgreSQL storage.
unverified: Production-composition replay against a real multi-gateway fleet.
Upstream permission refresh of an online observer that requires authority.

ci_findings_at_cfeb79fd: Test (windows-2025), run 37118322369: TestPromotionRequestLeaseLossLeavesTheRequest passed every assertion and then failed in the TempDir cleanup because state/.owner.lock was still open. Starmap Runtime.Close joins its shutdown for 5 s (closeJoinTimeout) and returns a typed TimeoutError while the cancelled work and the directory release continue. The harness cleanup discarded that error, and Windows refuses to remove a locked file. Unix unlinks an open file, so only Windows reports it. Fix: the harness cleanup closeRuntimeDirectory waits after a TimeoutError until the .owner.lock flock is free, bounded by promotionRunTimeout, and fails the test when the lock stays held. No assertion changed.
